newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber market thin due to currency woes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber market thin due to currency woes.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market closed quietly on Friday with the region's currency problems and the looming weekend keeping most of the trade on the sidelines, traders said.
"The focus of the market was still on the weak currencies in the region. It was a very thin market," a dealer said.
Thailand's decision to default on taking delivery of 23,100 tonnes of rubber was largely ignored by the market.
"Some people ignored the news. The market is still very nervous about the currency situation in the region," another dealer said.
Michelin, which has recently bought rubber as part of its monthly buying programme, was said to have asked for quotes in the market.
"I heard they asked for some quotes, but I think Michelin found the price a little too high," a dealer said.
"There was some shortcovering for RSS1 rubber, but volume in the rest of the market was fairly thin," a dealer said.
At 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 94.75 U.S. cents a kg from 94.00 cents. January/March RSS1 was seen at 154.25 Singapore cents (US$1.05 cents) a kg from 152.00 cents.
